Results of studies us- ing clodronate to reduce skeletal metastases in women with breast cancer have been conflicting,1,4-6 and one study in women with node-positive disease actually suggested an increase in con- comitant visceral metastases.5 Overall, the studies appeared lim- ited by duration, and further data are needed.7 In a trial of patients with multiple myeloma,8 oral clodronate was found to slow the progression of skeletal disease, especially in those patients with less overt disease at diagnosis; the authors suggested starting clodronate early in the course of the disease. 1. Clodronate has been reported to be of benefit in a boy with osteogenesis imperfecta (p.1083) type I. Starting at 13 ⁄ years old he was given oral clodronate 400 mg daily for 5 years, and sustained no new low-trauma fractures dur- ing this time.
